messages:
maya: Heads-up: Orchard tenant hitting repeated 429s on dedicated pool ded-pool-eu-west-2-03. Started 2026-03-15 17:02 UTC. Customer reports long chat sessions (~20-40k tokens) and rising p95. Ticket #98712. Logs show repeated kvcache evict spikes and slab alloc failures.

devon: Can you paste a small log snippet and confirm pool name? Any autoscale activity around the spike?

maya: Pool = ded-pool-eu-west-2-03. Logs (trimmed):
```
[17:01:03] kvcache: evicting 512MB entries; slab_free=2MB; fragmentation=0.78
[17:01:04] runtime: serve request tenant=orchard ctx_tokens=32000; latency=1.2s; status=429
[17:01:04] kvcache: alloc fail slab_realloc: cannot_allocate
```

liam: fragmentation=0.78 is pretty bad. That suggests lots of small free fragments. Could be sustained long-context entries preventing compaction. Any noisy neighbor activity reported?

maya: Customer says they had a handful of long-running summarization sessions, sustained but not a single huge embedding job.

priya: I pulled autoscaler logs around that window:
```
[16:59:50] autoscaler: desired_replicas=4 current=3
[17:00:10] autoscaler: scale_up -> 4 (pending GPU spinup)
[17:05:30] autoscaler: scale_up complete -> 4
```
So there was a ~5m gap where the pool ran with one fewer node. That plus fragmentation would push eviction to be aggressive and routers to throttle (429).

devon: Exactly. When underprovisioned we throttle to maintain SLOs. Two quick checks: is prefix caching enabled for Orchard? And what is their max_sequence? Those affect KV size.

maya: Orchard config shows prefix_cache: false and max_sequence: 65536 (they asked for long sequences for quality).

liam: OK. Actionable plan: (1) short-term toggle prefix_cache=true for tenant to reduce per-request KV growth, (2) schedule gentle slab compaction / rolling restart to defragment, (3) review autoscale triggers to scale earlier on sustained KV-driven mem pressure.

priya: Ops option to trigger compaction: `maintenancectl --pool ded-pool-eu-west-2-03 --compact-kv` — that'll do an in-place compaction and rejoin. Recommend low-traffic window.

ops-bot: Maintenance request for compaction submitted by priya. ETA 25m. Customer notified about brief reconnect. :white_check_mark:

maya: Customer agreed to the brief restart. Also asked about billing: they were charged for requests that returned 429 — they want a credit for those.

liam: Support: we'll credit failed requests. Opening finance follow-up.

devon: For the postmortem / follow-up engineering, gather: token length distribution, kv_entry_size histogram, slab_free trend, autoscale latency. I'll make a dashboard. Link: https://console.redwood/graphs/ded-pool-eu-west-2-03/kvcache (internal).

maya: Repro steps customer provided (simplified):
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
    -d '{"input":"<~30k token conversation>"}' \
    https://api.redwood.dev/v1/dedicated/orchard/generate &
done
wait
```
They run ~50 parallel clients with sequence windows ~30k.

priya: While we do the rolling restart, set tenant QoS burst=false so they don't re-fill the cache immediately during compaction.

devon: After compaction I'll run mem-profiling. If fragmentation stays >0.6 we need a runtime change: improve slab coalescing and consider a slab-resize heuristic. I'll raise RNW-612 for engineering work.

maya: I'll keep the customer updated and mark ticket 98712 with the mitigation steps. @liam please open the billing ticket. @devon please CC me on RNW-612.

liam: Billing ticket opened FT-3872 and assigned to finance-svc.

ops-bot: Compaction started at 17:24 UTC. Nodes draining, compaction in progress.

ops-bot: Compaction complete at 17:28 UTC; node rejoined pool. Post-restart metrics: p95 latency back to baseline, 429s dropped from ~10% -> 0.9%.

maya: Customer confirmed improvement and accepted a one-time credit offer. Proposed next steps documented: prefix_cache=true recommendation, autoscale threshold change (scale at 60% mem pressure vs current 80%), eng task RNW-612 to improve slab compaction/coalescing.

devon: I'll track RNW-612 and add a short-term patch to coalesce small KV allocations more aggressively. I'll post a design doc in eng-runtime.

maya: Thanks everyone. Closing loop with customer after RNW-612 gets initial PR. I'll update ticket 98712 and close once engineering has a concrete timeline.
